thread:
anya: Postmortem follow-up for today's model-router incident. We need clear owners for all external comms and a short redaction protocol before we publish anything public. I'll put a strawman below; please claim items or suggest changes by EOD today.

derek: thanks. can we also include an explicit ETA for the RCA? customers keep asking for timelines.

anya: yes. my suggestion: status page live update within 3 hours, targeted customer email within 12 hours, public RCA draft within 4 business days. open to adjustments.

priya: proposed status page blurb (short):

```
Incident: Model routing errors (partial)
Impact: Elevated inference latency & 502s affecting ~9% of requests from 08:05-08:42 UTC
Mitigation: Traffic reroute and instance reprovisioning reduced errors to <0.5% by 08:33 UTC
Next: Detailed RCA forthcoming; estimated publish: 4 business days
```

noah: looks good. suggest we add "customers on Dedicated may receive tailored comms" line if needed.

anya: good call. add one-liner: "Dedicated customers will receive direct notification if they were impacted."

priya: redaction protocol draft for customer-facing email / public RCA:
1) never include raw request_ids, tokens, or full traces.
2) aggregate counts only (no per-customer event counts).
3) scrub IPs and internal hostnames.
4) if we reference user-visible timestamps, round to minute blocks and avoid per-user timestamps.
5) legal sign-off required before publishing if any customer detects appear in the draft.

noah: I'll own the status page update. assigning to @noah. ETA: 3h.

anya: who will draft the dedicated-customer notification? we should avoid duplicating public phrasing.

derek: I can draft the dedicated note and coordinate with account teams. assigning to @derek. ETA: 12h.

priya: I'll take the public RCA draft (technical writeup) and include recurring-incident context; ETA: 4 business days. assigning to @priya.

legal-bot: Reminder: compliance checklist required. Submit draft for automated PII scan at https://legal.redwood.ai/scan.

anya: long-term remediation: platform infra to propose a routing backstop and improved health checks. who owns follow-through?

noah: platform can lead. I'll pair with infra and get a proposal in 10 business days. assigning to @noah for the remediation proposal.

anya: scheduling: let's also run a recurring-pattern retro to validate if this is a trend. propose invite to infra, platform, oncall, customer success. schedule within 2 weeks.

derek: I will coordinate scheduling. assigning to @derek.

priya: for the customer email, suggested structure: 1) brief timeline (what happened), 2) impact statement (who/what was affected), 3) mitigation actions taken, 4) RCA ETA and next steps, 5) contact for follow-up. keep it <200 words.

anya: +1. quick owner/timeline table (reply with :thumbsup: when you accept):
- Status page update -> owner: (assign); ETA -> 3 hours
- Dedicated customer notices -> owner: (assign); ETA -> 12 hours
- Public RCA draft -> owner: (assign); ETA -> 4 business days
- Remediation proposal (routing backstop) -> owner: (assign); ETA -> 10 business days
- Recurring-pattern retro -> owner: (assign); ETA -> schedule within 2 weeks

noah: :thumbsup: status page update accepted (@noah).

derek: :thumbsup: dedicated notices accepted (@derek).

priya: :thumbsup: public RCA accepted (@priya).

noah: status-bot: Incident digest posted to status.redwood.ai 1: status page update queued by @noah.

anya: I'll follow up with a short tracker doc (owners, ETA, status) and link it here. if any timeline slips, please update this thread. closing for active assignment tracking; reopen if changes needed. :white_check_mark:
